name: Demo Hotel CLT
label: Demo Hotel CLT · Tasteprint
description: A fictional Charlotte-area boutique-hotel demonstration. Every experience is illustrative; no affiliation, availability or booking is implied.

copy.title: Make a little room for your kind of stay.
copy.lede: A quiet reset, a new discovery, or an evening with good company. Eight small choices help you find an experience that fits the way you’d like to spend your time.
copy.catalogTitle: A few ideas for your stay
copy.catalogSubtitle: Illustrative experiences selected from this fictional hotel’s catalog. Nothing here is a real reservation or availability claim.

questions.title: You’ve checked in. What sounds good first?
questions.subtitle: Go with what would make this stay feel like yours.
options: Step outside and see something different.
A beautiful space, a good drink, a small detail.
Be around people and see where the day goes.

questions.title: How would you shape a free afternoon?
questions.subtitle: Choose the amount of structure that feels comfortable.
options: Know where I’m going, leave room around it.
Take an interesting turn without a schedule.
One easy thing, then time to do less.
A few stops and something active.

questions.title: What makes an evening feel special?
questions.subtitle: There’s no right way to spend it.
options: A table, someone close, no rush.
Something new with a story behind it.
Shared energy and a little spontaneity.
Call it a good day and recharge.

questions.title: What would you like this stay to give back?
questions.subtitle: Pick the feeling you’d most like to take home.
options: Rest can be the main event.
Notice things I wouldn’t at home.
Time with people is the point.

questions.title: Which small detail changes the experience?
questions.subtitle: Assume the basics are taken care of.
options: Less friction, more enjoying the moment.
Not every moment needs an itinerary.

questions.title: What kind of company fits this moment?
questions.subtitle: This is a preference, not a request for anyone’s details.
options: Space to follow my own pace.
I enjoy the possibility of new conversations.

questions.title: How would you start a free morning?
questions.subtitle: Think about enjoyment, not what you ought to do.
options: An active start, then a slower finish.
Take in the neighborhood at my pace.
A comfortable table and time to linger.

questions.title: Choose the tradeoff you’d be happiest making.
questions.subtitle: The useful part is knowing what matters more.
options: I’m happy to miss some action for a restorative pause.
A little uncertainty is part of discovery.
A clear, considered experience helps me relax.
Leave room for the evening to develop.

catalog.name: A quiet courtyard pause
catalog.description: A tucked-away seat, a book and a little space to let the day settle. A fictional example of a restorative in-hotel offering.
catalog.tradeoff: A good fit for slowing down; less suited to a high-energy afternoon.

catalog.name: Breakfast, without the rush
catalog.description: A considered breakfast setting and time to linger. An illustrative way a hotel could make an ordinary morning feel personal.
catalog.tradeoff: Comfort and atmosphere come first, rather than novelty or a packed schedule.

catalog.name: A neighborhood art wander
catalog.description: A self-paced look at neighborhood art and design. This is a fictional itinerary concept, not a named venue, partner or guided tour.
catalog.tradeoff: Best when you have energy to explore; specific access and conditions would need checking.

catalog.name: An active morning, your way
catalog.description: A gentle-to-active morning outing concept with room to choose your pace. Not a prescribed workout or a verified local route.
catalog.tradeoff: Movement is the draw; weather, route access and your own needs would shape the real choice.

catalog.name: An evening with a little buzz
catalog.description: A welcoming lounge setting and space for easy conversation. A fictional social offering, without an event schedule or alcohol requirement.
catalog.tradeoff: Shared energy comes with more stimulation; choose a quieter idea if you want to recharge.

catalog.name: A small tasting, a good story
catalog.description: A hosted tasting concept focused on craft, flavor and the story behind it. No menu, dietary suitability or reservation is promised.
catalog.tradeoff: More structured than wandering; dietary needs and actual offering details must be confirmed.
